title: A warm answer allows another perspective

captions.physics: Returning to a question heard anew

meaning: You can return to a question heard anew and answer openly, experiencing an unfamiliar suspended conclusion without immediately replacing it with a final new assessment.
text: Judgement in the physical position of your Vishuddha appears in returning to a question now heard differently. The Sun in energy supports a wish to answer openly and kindly and name actual substance. The Hanged Man in emotions brings unfamiliarity in a suspended conclusion. You can answer clarification about a word instead of defending a general position. Another perspective guarantees no immediate ease even while conversation stays warm.

For example, you return to “Why did you call that a mistake?” Earlier you wanted to defend against disagreement; now a question about a chosen word’s meaning becomes clear. **An open answer leaves another perspective time**. You can say, “I meant one inaccurate phrase rather than the entire exchange”. Yet a familiar general assessment is suspended. Hesitation emerges because your own expression now needs to be viewed differently. It proves neither absent thought nor hidden refusal to discuss; substance already has a more precise form.

Difficulty arises if friendliness means immediately feeling comfortable in another perspective. Awkwardness seems evidence of an insincere answer. Constructive Sun energy helps preserve clear participation alongside actual feeling. You can explain a word while getting used to another view; warmth is not measured by inward change’s speed, while new understanding requires neither abandoning every earlier assessment nor immediately replacing them with one flawlessly pleasant formulation.
